title: Love your family, but do not let them pull you from faith.
subtitle: When closeness becomes a pull away from Allah
then: In those years, families in Arabia were split: a son believing, a father fighting him. The believers were told not to take as {trap}allies and confidants{/trap} relatives who had chosen disbelief over faith and stood against it. Ibn Kathir links it to {idea}"You will not find a people who believe in Allah... loving those who oppose Allah."{/idea}
now: Your family wants you to skip Jumuah for the reunion, or mocks your hijab, or pushes you toward a deal you know is wrong. You can stay kind and present. {idea}What you cannot do is let their pull decide your faith for you.{/idea}
old: Keeping my family happy comes before everything.
new: I can honor my family and still refuse to let them pull me from Allah.
try: Next time family pressure clashes with your faith, answer with warmth and a clear no.

title: Eight loves on one side, Allah on the other.
subtitle: A checklist of what holds your heart
then: As the believers were called to give and strive, this verse listed {reward}everything a person naturally loves{/reward} and asked which was dearer. Ibn Kathir adds the moment Umar said the Prophet ﷺ was dearer to him than all but himself, and was told faith means {idea}more than yourself too{/idea}. Then Umar said: now you are.
now: Read the list slowly: your parents, your kids, your partner, your savings, your business, your flat you finally decorated. {idea}None is wrong to love.{/idea} The test is the moment one of them asks you to put Allah second. Which one would win?
old: I love Allah most, I just never get asked to prove it.
new: When my loves clash with Allah, the one I choose shows what is first.
try: Read the list in the verse and honestly mark which item would most easily pull you away.

title: Your large numbers pleased you, and gave you nothing.
subtitle: The lesson of Hunayn
then: In the eighth year, just after Makkah, a Muslim army of about twelve thousand marched to Hunayn. {trap}They were pleased with their numbers.{/trap} Hawazin ambushed them in the valley and most fled. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ stayed firm{/idea}, calling out: I am the Prophet, no lie.
now: A full team, a big budget, a strong CV, a big family behind you. You walk in sure it cannot go wrong, and it does. {idea}Prepare well, but put your trust in Allah, not in the size of what you have.{/idea}
old: With all this behind me, I cannot fail.
new: No amount of people or resources replaces relying on Allah.
try: Before your next big task, say a short dua asking Allah for success instead of counting your advantages.

title: Then came calm from Allah, and help no one saw.
subtitle: Sakinah after panic
then: Al-Abbas called out to the companions of the Pledge under the Tree, and the fleeing Muslims answered: here we are. They returned to the Prophet ﷺ. Allah then {reward}sent down His calm on His Messenger and the believers{/reward}, and {reward}soldiers they did not see.{/reward}
now: The test results come back bad. The business collapses. Your mind races and you want to run. {idea}Turn back toward Allah, even after a first panic.{/idea} Calm is something He sends down; ask for it.
old: Once I have panicked and failed, it is too late.
new: Even after I run, I can turn back, and Allah can send calm.
try: In your next anxious moment, stop and ask Allah for sakinah by name.

title: After the battle, the door of repentance stayed open.
subtitle: Yesterday's opponent, forgiven

row.title: Allah may still turn to them

then: Right after describing the defeat of those who fought at Hunayn, the verse adds: {reward}after that, Allah turns in mercy to whom He wills.{/reward} The ones who had just been fighting the believers were not shut out from forgiveness.
now: You lost the argument badly, or you were the one in the wrong. The defeat feels like the end of the story. {idea}It does not have to be.{/idea} After the loss comes the chance to turn back to Allah.
old: After what I did, there is no coming back.
new: Even after a failure or defeat, Allah's forgiveness is still on offer.
try: Think of a recent failure. Turn it into one sincere istighfar today.

title: Afraid of losing income? Allah will enrich you.
subtitle: When doing right threatens your livelihood
then: In the ninth year, it was ruled that after that season the idolaters would no longer come to the Sacred Mosque. Ibn Ishaq reports the people's fear: {trap}our markets will close and our earnings will vanish.{/trap} The reply: {reward}Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills.{/reward}
now: Your biggest client wants you to cut a corner. Refusing could cost you the account, the rent, the school fees. {reward}The verse speaks straight to that fear{/reward}: your provision was never in that one door.
old: If I do the right thing, I will lose my income.
new: My provision comes from Allah, who has more doors than I can see.
try: Name one money fear that keeps you from doing right. Say: Allah will enrich me from His bounty.

title: The call that led to Tabuk, in drought and heat.
subtitle: The setting of the hard march north
then: Ibn Kathir places this verse in the ninth year, when the command came to fight the People of the Book and the Prophet ﷺ prepared to march against the Romans. {trap}It was a year of drought and intense heat.{/trap} About thirty thousand marched to Tabuk, camped about twenty days, and returned. {trap}Some, including hypocrites, stayed behind.{/trap}
now: The hard call never comes in an easy season. The parent needs care during your busiest year. The fast comes in the longest days. {idea}This part of the surah is about who answers when it costs something{/idea}, and you are asked that question in your own life.
old: I will answer Allah's call once things get easier.
new: The call that matters often comes in the hardest season. That is the test.
try: Do one act of obedience today that you have been postponing until life is less busy.

title: Words from the mouth, with no proof behind them.
subtitle: Saying things about Allah without knowledge
then: The verse addresses claims made at the time that Allah had a son, {trap}"a saying from their mouths"{/trap}, Ibn Kathir explains, with no proof, {trap}imitating what earlier peoples had said.{/trap} The surah answers it with pure tawhid: Allah alone, without partner or child.
now: You repeat something about Allah you heard on a video or from an uncle: "Allah will never forgive that," "this dua guarantees anything." Is it from Allah, or just from mouths? {idea}Check what you say about Allah before you say it.{/idea}
old: If many people say it about Allah, it must be right.
new: What I say about Allah needs to come from Him, not from repetition.
try: Pick one belief you hold about Allah. Look up its source in the Quran or a sound hadith.

title: Obeying people over Allah is a form of worship.
subtitle: The question Adi bin Hatim asked
then: Adi bin Hatim, chief of Tayy, came to Madinah and heard this verse. He said: they did not worship their scholars. The Prophet ﷺ replied that {trap}they made lawful what was forbidden and forbade what was lawful, and people followed{/trap}. {idea}That obedience was the worship.{/idea} Adi accepted Islam that day.
now: Your boss, your favorite influencer, your friend group, even a popular preacher. When one of them says something Allah made clear is fine is wrong, or the reverse, and you go along without thinking, {idea}ask whose word you are really following.{/idea}
old: As long as I do not bow to anyone, I am worshipping only Allah.
new: Whoever I obey over Allah in what is lawful and unlawful, I have raised up.
try: Think of one thing you do only because someone you admire says so. Check what Allah says about it.

title: Blowing at the sun to put it out.
subtitle: Allah's light will be completed

row.title: Allah perfects it
sub: my job is to walk in it

then: Ibn Kathir says those who tried to put out the guidance with {trap}argument and lies{/trap} are like {trap}someone blowing at the sun or the moon to extinguish it.{/trap} He also notes kafir comes from covering, like night covering things or a farmer covering seed.
now: You read a viral thread mocking Islam and feel your stomach drop, as if the truth itself is in danger. {reward}It is not.{/reward} Allah will complete His light. {idea}Your part is to keep it lit in your own home and heart.{/idea}
old: Every attack on the faith makes me afraid it will fade.
new: Allah has promised to complete His light. I only need to walk in it.
try: Instead of scrolling one more argument online, read one page of Quran today.

title: Sent with guidance and the religion of truth.
subtitle: What the Messenger ﷺ brought
then: Ibn Kathir explains guidance as {idea}the true reports and beneficial faith{/idea} the Prophet ﷺ brought, and the religion of truth as {idea}the righteous deeds that benefit in this life and the next.{/idea} Tamim Ad-Dari, once a Christian, said he saw goodness and honor come to those of his people who accepted it.
now: You may never shape what happens on a world stage. But there is a small territory you do govern: your tongue, your phone, your mornings. {idea}Let the guidance prevail there first.{/idea}
old: Islam's success is about what happens far away from me.
new: The guidance prevails first in the life I actually run.
try: Choose one habit today and bring it in line with what the Prophet ﷺ taught.
